PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-09-20
57M, general wellness examination.

S:
Patient presents for his yearly examination. Reports feeling well overall. Works full time in a warehouse, often 9 to 10 hour shifts, and walks on weekends. Takes his blood pressure medication every morning and checks readings at home twice a week. Sleeps 7 hours most nights. Appetite good, weight stable. Patient denies depression. Enjoys time with his grandchildren on weekends and reports good support at home. Father with heart failure. Never smoker, rare alcohol. No new concerns today. Asks about vaccines he is due for.

O:
BP 126/78, HR 68, RR 14, Temp 98.3 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 186 lb, BMI 26.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, pulses intact.
Labs (prior week): basic metabolic panel normal, lipid panel within goal, A1c 5.4%.
PHQ-2 score 0.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home readings reviewed, averaging 124/78. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. Family history: discussed father's history with patient. Reviewed warning signs such as new shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, or reduced exercise tolerance, and to call if any develop.
3. Health maintenance: colorectal screening up to date. Shingles vaccine discussed; patient will schedule. Influenza vaccine given today. Encouraged continued weekend walking and adding light strength exercises twice weekly.

Return in 12 months for next wellness visit, sooner as needed.
